final_answer: Hypothesis: Increased education spending does not positively impact per capita GDP in either Sub-Saharan Africa or Lower Middle Income Countries. The relationship is negative, suggesting that higher education spending is associated with lower per capita GDP in these regions. This hypothesis is derived from the dataset, which includes variables such as 'Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI)' and 'GNI per capita (constant 2015 USdollar)'. The analysis showed a strong negative relationship in Sub-Saharan Africa (coefficient: -159.13, R-squared: 0.934) and a weak negative relationship in Lower Middle Income Countries (coefficient: -635.07, R-squared: 0.231).
